# Pai.pt Business Directory Scraper

Pai.pt (Páginas Amarelas) is Portugal's long-running business directory. This actor turns its
public search results and company pages into a clean dataset of Portuguese businesses: contact
details, addresses, map coordinates, opening hours, ratings, services, photos and the categories
the directory uses.

You can start from a keyword such as `canalizador`, from one of the common category slugs, from
several cities at once, or by pasting search and profile URLs you already built on the site. Every
record is emitted as-is from the directory; fields the directory does not publish are left out
instead of being filled with empty placeholders.

## What you can do

- Search by free-text keyword, by category slug, or both across several cities, districts and
  islands in one run.
- Read all result pages of each search, or cap pages per search with `maxPages`.
- Sort by pai.pt's ranking or by popularity, and keep only businesses open now or above a minimum
  rating.
- Enrich each result from its profile page with email, website, social links, all phone numbers,
  coordinates, rating and review count, services, payment methods, amenities, gallery images and
  the business's own description.
- Paste search URLs, category pages or individual profile URLs to reproduce a manual browse.
- Pass a public pai.pt listings sitemap URL in `startUrls` to enumerate business profiles beyond a
  single search's 500-row cap.
- Get stable identifiers and canonical `www.pai.pt` profile links for every business.

## Output fields

Each dataset item is one business. The actor omits a field whenever pai.pt has no value for it.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `listingId` | Numeric pai.pt listing id, taken from the profile URL |
| `name` | Business name |
| `category` | Category label shown on the search-result card |
| `cardDescription` | Short tagline from the search card, when it differs from the name |
| `categories` | Categories registered on the business profile |
| `categoryPath` | Breadcrumb path shown on the profile, e.g. `comer & beber > restaurantes` |
| `tags` | Keyword tags registered on the profile |
| `verticals` | Pai.pt industry vertical(s) |
| `description` | The business's own "about" text |
| `street`, `postalCode`, `city`, `country`, `fullAddress` | Postal address |
| `latitude`, `longitude` | Map coordinates |
| `phone` | Primary phone number |
| `phones` | Every distinct phone number found on the profile |
| `phoneDetails` | Phone numbers with the call-cost note shown by pai.pt |
| `email` | Primary published email |
| `emails` | Every published email |
| `website` | Primary external website (or the first link when only social pages exist) |
| `websites` | External non-social website links |
| `socialLinks` | Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and other social links |
| `imageUrl` | Main profile image |
| `imageUrls` | Gallery and service images found on the profile |
| `logoUrl` | Business logo, when published |
| `openingHours` | Structured weekly windows (`weekday`, `day`, `open`, `close`) |
| `openingHoursText` | One-line weekly schedule |
| `isOpenNow` | Whether the business is open now in the Europe/Lisbon timezone |
| `rating` | Average rating, only when the business has reviews |
| `reviewCount` | Number of reviews behind `rating` |
| `services` | Services listed in the profile's services block |
| `menuSections` | Menu-section headings such as "Pratos de Peixe" or "Sobremesas" |
| `paymentMethods` | Payment methods listed under "Métodos de Pagamento" |
| `specialHours` | Special-hours labels such as "Aberto 24h" or "Aberto aos Sábados" |
| `amenities` | Amenities listed under "Comodidades" |
| `restaurantFeatures` | Restaurant features listed on the profile |
| `idealFor` | "Ideal Para" labels |
| `mealPrices` | Meal-price labels |
| `mealTypes` | Meal-type labels |
| `specialties` | Specialty labels |
| `deliveryConditions` | Delivery-condition labels |
| `features` | Any other profile feature group, keyed by its original heading |
| `isSponsored` | `true` when the result card is a sponsored placement |
| `searchQuery` | Keyword that produced this record (keyword searches) |
| `searchCategory` | Category that produced this record (category searches) |
| `searchLocation` | Location that produced this record |
| `sourceUrl` | Canonical pai.pt profile URL |
| `recordType` | Always `business` |
| `scrapedAt` | UTC timestamp of the scrape |

## Input fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `search` | `search` for keyword/category results, `detail` for profile URLs only. |
| `searchQueries` | array | `[]` | Free-text keywords. Each keyword is searched in every location. |
| `categories` | array | `[]` | Category slugs for multi-category runs. Takes priority over `category`. |
| `category` | string | `restaurantes` | A common category, or `custom` to use `customCategory`. |
| `customCategory` | string | - | Category slug used when the category fields are empty. |
| `locations` | array | `[]` | City, district or island names for multi-location runs. |
| `location` | string | Any location (nationwide) | A curated city/concelho, or `custom` to use `customLocation`. |
| `customLocation` | string | - | Location name used when the location fields are empty. |
| `sortBy` | string | `ranked` | `ranked` (pai.pt ranking) or `popular`. |
| `openNowOnly` | boolean | `false` | Keep only businesses open now; unknown hours are kept. |
| `minRating` | string | No minimum | `1`-`5`; businesses without a rating are kept. |
| `startUrls` | array | `[]` | Pai.pt search, category or profile URLs, or a public listings sitemap URL. |
| `fetchDetails` | boolean | `true` | Visit each profile for email, website, coordinates, rating, services and gallery. |
| `maxItems` | integer | `20` | Maximum records across the whole run (1-2000). |
| `maxPages` | integer | `50` | Maximum result pages per search (1-500). |

`mode`, `searchQueries`, `categories`, `locations` and `startUrls` can be combined. Searches are
fanned out across every keyword/category and location pair, and duplicates are removed by pai.pt
listing id. When `startUrls` are supplied, the single `category`/`location` defaults are ignored so
profile or search URLs are not mixed with an unintended default search; use the `categories` and
`locations` arrays if you want to add searches alongside URLs.

## Examples

Keyword search in two cities, with profiles:

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "searchQueries": ["canalizador", "eletricista"],
  "locations": ["Lisboa", "Porto"],
  "maxItems": 100,
  "fetchDetails": true
}
```

Category search across several municipalities:

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "categories": ["restaurantes", "hoteis"],
  "locations": ["Lisboa", "Cascais", "Sintra"],
  "sortBy": "popular",
  "maxItems": 200
}
```

Fast card-only scan, open businesses rated 4+:

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "category": "dentistas",
  "location": "",
  "openNowOnly": true,
  "minRating": "4",
  "fetchDetails": false,
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

Paste a search URL or profile URLs:

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "startUrls": [
    { "url": "https://www.pai.pt/searches?search[query]=canalizador&search[location]=Lisboa&search[location_id]=20477" },
    { "url": "https://www.pai.pt/paginas/691542-hidroclean-canalizacao" }
  ],
  "maxItems": 20
}
```

Full-directory enumeration beyond one search's cap:

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "startUrls": [
    { "url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/poetic-primer-235017.appspot.com/public/listings.xml.gz" }
  ],
  "maxItems": 2000
}
```

## Use cases

- Build a Portuguese trade or service lead list with phone, email and website.
- Compare business density and ratings for a trade across municipalities.
- Keep a CRM or local-search product supplied with structured directory records.
- Find businesses open now or above a rating threshold for a specific area.
- Refresh a list of company profiles by pasting their pai.pt URLs.

## FAQ and limits

**Does this need a login or API key?** No. It reads public pages only.

**Why are some fields missing?** Pai.pt only publishes some data on some profiles. Ratings appear
after reviews, email is not universal, and not every business has services or feature groups. The
actor omits missing values rather than inventing them.

**How many results can one search return?** Pai.pt caps a search at 500 businesses (50 pages of
10). The actor reads up to `maxPages` per search; to go beyond 500, split by category, keyword or
location. Multi-location and multi-category runs partition the space automatically and deduplicate.
The run status warns when a search hits the cap. For a full-directory listing, pass the public
`listings.xml.gz` sitemap URL in `startUrls`; that path enumerates profile URLs outside the search
cap.

**Can I search around a latitude/longitude?** Not as a standalone mode. Pai.pt's map bounds only
filter a search that already has a location id, so the public site does not offer a true radius
search. Use a city/district, then filter the returned coordinates yourself if needed.

**How do I search a district or island?** Use the full name, e.g. `Distrito de Braga`, `Regi?o de
Lisboa`, `Ilha da Madeira` or `Ilha de S?o Miguel`, in `locations`/`customLocation`. For the Azores,
use individual island names rather than the archipelago name.

**Why does `dentistas` with a city return little?** Pai.pt files individual dentists under the
broader medical category and only tags them with "dentista"; the nationwide keyword still resolves.
For a city, search `clinicas-e-especialidades-medicas` or use a keyword query.

**What if a location name is not found?** The actor resolves names through pai.pt's own location
suggestions. Unresolved locations are reported in the run status instead of silently returning
nationwide data.

**Are ratings always present?** No. They are published only for businesses with reviews; absent
ratings are omitted, never written as zero.

**Are menu items or review text included?** The public profile exposes menu-section headings but not
the dish bodies/prices, and it exposes the rating/count but not the review text. Those fields are
omitted rather than guessed.

**Do image links work everywhere?** Image URLs point at pai.pt's image host. If that host blocks
your network, the profile page URL is still available; the actor does not rehost images by default.

**What happens when pai.pt blocks a request?** The actor tries a direct request first, then a
public mirror, then Apify's datacenter proxy. No proxy setup is required from you.

**Is this affiliated with pai.pt?** No. It reads publicly available pages and is independent of
Páginas Amarelas.

## Data source

Public search and business-profile pages on `www.pai.pt`. The actor stores canonical profile URLs
and does not require cookies, accounts or user-supplied credentials.
